title: Hepatic cavernous hemangioma: malformation of vascular channels
vignette: A 36-year-old man undergoes right hemicolectomy due to adenocarcinoma arising from the hepatic flexure. He has a prolonged history of ulcerative colitis; periodic surveillance colonoscopy was recommended, but the patient was not adherent. During the operation, a liver lesion is also resected. Microscopic examination of the liver lesion shows cavernous, blood-filled vascular spaces of variable size, lined by a single layer of flat endothelial cells and separated by thin fibrous septa, without cytologic atypia. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's liver lesion?

clues.text: a liver lesion is also resected
clues.note: An incidentally found liver lesion in a colon-cancer patient raises the question of metastasis vs a benign lesion - the histology distinguishes them.

clues.text: cavernous, blood-filled vascular spaces of variable size, lined by a single layer of flat endothelial cells and separated by thin fibrous septa, without cytologic atypia
clues.note: Dilated blood-filled vascular spaces lined by bland flat endothelium with thin fibrous septa (no atypia) = cavernous HEMANGIOMA, a benign vascular malformation.

whatMatters: Cavernous, blood-filled vascular spaces lined by a single layer of bland flat ENDOTHELIUM with thin fibrous septa (no cytologic atypia) = CAVERNOUS HEMANGIOMA - the most common benign liver tumor, thought to be a congenital MALFORMATION OF VASCULAR CHANNELS. Answer B. (Not a colon metastasis - that would show atypical glands.)
strategy: Read the histology: benign dilated vascular channels lined by flat endothelium = cavernous hemangioma (vascular malformation). Reject the malignant/other options that don't match bland vascular spaces: metastatic colonic adenocarcinoma (atypical glands, not vascular spaces), hepatocellular carcinoma (atypical hepatocyte plates), cholangiocarcinoma (atypical bile-duct glands in fibrous stroma), and primary sclerosing cholangitis (onion-skin periductal fibrosis).

options.text: Chronic obliterative inflammation of bile ducts
Neoplastic proliferation of intrahepatic bile ducts

eliminations.label: Chronic obliterative bile duct inflammation - primary sclerosing cholangitis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: concentric periductal ('onion-skin') fibrosis of bile ducts = primary sclerosing cholangitis (associated with ulcerative colitis). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this lesion is a vascular tumor (blood-filled spaces), not a biliary process. ✅ Correct if: onion-skin bile-duct fibrosis with cholestasis.

eliminations.label: Malignant hepatocyte proliferation - hepatocellular carcinoma
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: hepatocellular carcinoma - thickened plates of atypical hepatocytes (in chronic liver disease). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the histology shows bland vascular spaces, not atypical hepatocytes. ✅ Correct if: hepatocyte plates with cytologic atypia and cirrhosis.

eliminations.label: Metastasis from colonic neoplasm - atypical glands (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the liver is the most common site of colon-cancer metastasis, which shows atypical elongated hyperchromatic glands. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this lesion is composed of bland vascular channels lined by flat endothelium - a hemangioma, not adenocarcinoma glands. ✅ Correct if: histology showed malignant glandular epithelium.

eliminations.label: Neoplastic intrahepatic bile ducts - cholangiocarcinoma
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: cholangiocarcinoma - infiltrative atypical glands in a dense fibrous (desmoplastic) stroma. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is a glandular malignancy, not the bland vascular spaces seen here. ✅ Correct if: atypical bile-duct glands in fibrous stroma.

reasoning: Liver lesion histology: dilated blood-filled vascular spaces lined by a single flat endothelial layer, thin fibrous septa, no atypia
This is a cavernous hemangioma - the most common benign liver tumor
Cavernous hemangiomas are congenital malformations of vascular channels
-> malformation of vascular channels; answer B
mechanism: Cavernous HEMANGIOMA is the MOST COMMON BENIGN liver tumor in adults. It is thought to be a congenital VASCULAR MALFORMATION - abnormal, dilated (cavernous) vascular channels that enlarge over time by ectasia (dilation from structural weakening or increased pressure), rather than by neoplastic proliferation or hyperplasia. Grossly it is a small, well-circumscribed, blood-filled, red-brown 'spongy' mass; microscopically it shows variably sized, blood-filled cavernous VASCULAR SPACES lined by a SINGLE layer of flat, bland ENDOTHELIAL cells and separated by thin FIBROUS SEPTA, without cytologic atypia. Most are asymptomatic and found incidentally (as here, during surgery for another reason); prognosis is excellent, and resection is reserved for symptomatic/large lesions (biopsy is generally avoided due to bleeding risk). Its bland vascular histology distinguishes it from the malignant possibilities in a colon-cancer patient: metastatic colonic adenocarcinoma (atypical glands), hepatocellular carcinoma (atypical hepatocyte plates), and cholangiocarcinoma (atypical bile-duct glands in fibrous stroma); primary sclerosing cholangitis (associated with ulcerative colitis) shows onion-skin periductal fibrosis, not a vascular tumor.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Path/GI > cavernous hemangioma: most common benign liver tumor; congenital vascular malformation; cavernous blood-filled spaces lined by flat endothelium + fibrous septa; avoid biopsy (bleeding).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Bland vascular channels lined by flat endothelium = hemangioma (vascular malformation), not colon metastasis.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on cavernous hemangioma, vascular malformation, endothelial lining, ectasia, or cytologic atypia? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Metastasis/HCC/cholangiocarcinoma show atypical glands/hepatocytes; primary sclerosing cholangitis = onion-skin bile ducts.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the histology: variably sized blood-filled (red) vascular spaces lined by a single flat endothelial layer, separated by thin pink fibrous septa, no atypia. Anchor: 'cavernous blood-filled spaces + flat endothelium = hemangioma (vascular malformation).'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: hepatic cavernous hemangioma = most common benign liver tumor; congenital vascular malformation; don't biopsy (bleeding).

keywords.front: Blood-filled vascular spaces lined by flat endothelium + fibrous septa (liver)
Why avoid biopsy of a hemangioma

firstAid.detail: Path: benign vascular malformation; blood-filled spaces + flat endothelium; most common benign liver tumor.
Path > metastasis (glands), HCC (hepatocytes), cholangiocarcinoma, PSC (bile ducts).
GI > incidental, asymptomatic; avoid biopsy; resect if large/symptomatic.

memoryHook: Sponge full of blood lined with plain endothelium and no atypia = cavernous hemangioma - a benign vascular birthmark of the liver, not a colon-cancer spread.
